end.name: SUMED (Arab Petroleum Pipelines Co.) Ain Sokhna terminal
end.coord_basis: Ain Sukhna port coordinates, 29°38'0"N 32°20'0"E, from a maritime port-info database

sheet_conflicts: ZafMarine's own project page describes the pipeline as connecting 'offshore production platforms to the SUMED (Suez-Mediterranean) pipeline network' — generic phrasing, not explicitly the FSRU import route. Given the exact 12 km / offshore-Gulf-of-Suez / SUMED match, and that SUMED Port, Ain Sokhna is independently reported (Daily News Egypt) to host FSRU marine-berth gas-import infrastructure feeding the national grid, the most likely read is that this is that offshore-to-terminal leg — but the two sources don't use identical terms for the same asset, so treat the FSRU-specific framing as an inference, not a directly stated fact.
notes: ZafMarine (marine/subsea contractor) completed a 12 km, 24-inch subsea gas pipeline in the Gulf of Suez for SUMED on 15 March 2025 ('completed two weeks ahead of schedule, with zero safety incidents') — length matches the sheet's 12.0 km exactly, and status (recent construction) is consistent with the sheet. Two independent sources corroborate the general SUMED Port / Ain Sokhna gas-import corridor (ZafMarine + Daily News Egypt), though only ZafMarine gives the specific 12 km figure and its own contractor framing ('offshore production platforms' rather than 'FSRU'). Start coordinate is the FSRU terminal position from Global Energy Observatory (an independent, non-GEM legacy database); end coordinate is the general SUMED/Ain Sokhna terminal position from a port database — neither source discusses this specific pipeline by name, so they support the coordinates only, not the routing claim itself (that rests on ZafMarine + Daily News Egypt).

No source found naming a distinct 6.1 km 'SUMED Gas Pipeline' with its own endpoints. Corridor hypothesis only: GASCO (engineering/PM) and Petrojet (construction) built marine and onshore pipelines at SUMED Port, Ain Sokhna to carry regasified LNG from the FSRU marine berth into the national gas grid (Egyptian Gazette, Daily News Egypt) — P8005 is plausibly the short onshore continuation of P8004's offshore leg (SUMED terminal landfall to a national-grid tie-in point a few km inland), but no source states a distinct length, a named tie-in facility, or its own coordinate. Recommend a follow-up pass with fresh search budget: Egypt Oil & Gas / Enterprise Press archives, GASCO project pages, or Arabic search ('خط أنابيب سوميد للغاز', 'الشبكة القومية') targeting the onshore segment specifically.

start.name: Sonker Bulk Liquids Terminal, Basin 3, Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Wikipedia coordinate for Ain Sokhna port/town (29°36'00"N 32°19'00"E) — general port-area location only; Sonker's Basin 3 terminal sits within Ain Sokhna/Sokhna Port but no more precise public coordinate was found for the jetty itself

notes: Sonker (Sonker Bunkering Company / Sonker Energy) operates the Bulk Liquids Terminal at Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Gulf of Suez — a site that berths FSRUs and feeds regasified LNG into Egypt's national gas grid via dedicated pipelines built 'outside the port fence' (IFC ESRS disclosure, re: an adjacent line as an analogue). Two FSRUs began operating from Sonker in 2015 -- Hoegh Gallant (March, 500 MMSCFD) and BW Singapore (November, 750 MMSCFD) (Sonker company history page) -- a plausible basis for GEM's 'Phase 1'/'Phase 2' gas-line split (one grid tie-in per FSRU), but no source names which phase is 9 km vs 7 km, nor identifies the specific national-grid valve/metering station each ties into. A separate, later (2025) GASCO/Petrojet gas-import pipeline (17 km, 36-inch, 3 valve rooms, built by Petrojet) for a third FSRU at Sonker is documented in the two Daily News Egypt articles -- that is a newer, distinct project, not P8006/P8007. Could not source a specific end-point name/coordinate for either phase this session (WebSearch budget exhausted mid-task, shared across concurrent research). Recommend a follow-up pass targeting GASCO's network map / EIA filings to pin the tie-in point, and to determine which phase is 9 km vs 7 km.

end.name: Ras Bakr Transmission Station
end.coord_basis: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Ra's Bakr' (point feature, N28 23'31" E33 3'42"), Red Sea Governorate, Egypt -- the nearest named public gazetteer entry to the transmission station named in the trade-press source below; GeoNames also separately lists a 'Ra's Bakr' oilfield ~14 km further NW (N28 29'0" E32 57'0"), confirming this as a real, long-standing place name in the Ras Gharib oil/gas cluster, not a typo

sheet_conflicts: Sheet StartLocation 'Petreco Plant' is confirmed as an accurate, verbatim name (not a misspelling) -- it appears exactly as 'Petreco Plant' in the source table below. EndLocation is currently blank on the sheet and should be 'Ras Bakr Transmission Station'.
notes: Egypt Oil & Gas Newspaper's Sept 2020 report 'Gulf of Suez, Eastern Desert and Sinai: Egypt's Crude Oil Squad' (PDF) contains a table 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Gulf of Suez/Sinai' listing seven pipelines; one row reads exactly: 'Trans Gulf Gas | Petreco Plant | Ras Bakr Transmission Station | 75 km | 12 in | 110 mmcf/d' -- an exact match to the sheet's 75.0 km length and StartLocation text. Body text independently confirms: 'Two of the seven pipelines (i.e. Trans Gulf Gas and Zaafarana-Korimat pipelines) transport natural gas to be pumped in two stations: Ras Bakr Transmission Station and Korimat Power Station.' NOTE ON VERIFICATION: url_verifier.py FAILs this URL on the 'Trans Gulf' substring check because the source is an embedded-text PDF whose two-column table layout the extractor doesn't parse cleanly -- this is the documented PDF-extraction false-negative case, not evidence the page is dead/wrong. I downloaded the PDF via WebFetch and ran `pdftotext -layout` and `pdftotext` (no layout) locally myself; both cleanly show 'Petreco Plant' / 'Ras Bakr' / 'Transmission Station' as contiguous text, confirming the table content directly rather than relying on the substring screen. Could not independently geocode 'Petreco Plant' itself -- no gazetteer, company database, or press mention of a facility by that name was found in GeoNames or the sources reachable this session (WebSearch tool quota was exhausted session-wide before this could be searched further; site/company-name searches via direct WebFetch on Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo all failed on bot-detection). Recommend a follow-up pass with fresh search budget for 'Petreco' as a company/plant name in the Ras Gharib gas-processing cluster (candidates worth checking: GPC, Petrobel/Belayim, Petrozeit, Petrogulf -- several similarly-named JVs operate gas processing in this exact area per Suez Oil Company's own facilities page). Until then this PID should stay resolved:false since only one endpoint has a real coordinate.

end.coord_basis: VesselFinder port database entry for Ras Shukheir, Egypt (28.1339 N, 33.2814 E); corroborated by a second independent maritime database (portcode.net, GUPCO Ras Shukheir entry, ~28.134 N, 33.267 E)

notes: Confirms the hint: Egypt Oil & Gas Newspaper's Sept 2020 report table 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Gulf of Suez/Sinai' lists 'Zeit Bay-Ras Shukheir (Pre-2017) | Zeit Bay | Ras Shukheir | 40 km | 16 in | 140 mmcf/d' -- an exact match to the sheet's 40.0 km length and pipeline name. Independently, Suez Oil Company's (SUCO -- the EGPC/RWE DEA joint venture operating Zeit Bay) own production-facilities page states: 'Zeit Bay Gas Plant ... The LPG product is sent via 6" pipeline to GUPCO Ras Shukier storage area for distribution' -- a second, independent primary-operator source confirming a real pipeline on this exact corridor (note: this SUCO-described 6-inch LPG line and the newspaper's 16-inch, 40 km gas trunk line are probably not the identical pipe -- likely a smaller product line vs. the larger gas trunk -- but both corroborate that Zeit Bay and Ras Shukheir are connected by real, named pipeline infrastructure, which is what P8015 requires). Two independent sources for each endpoint's coordinate (SeaRates for Zeit Bay Terminal; VesselFinder + portcode.net for Ras Shukheir) and two independent sources for the pipeline's existence/length (Egypt Oil & Gas trade press + SUCO's own site, the latter cited in prose only per the note above).
